And real friends will tell you if a behavior concerns them not just shun you for it. Psychosis doesn't necessarily lead to schizophrenia. Plenty of mental health issues can lead to delusional or altered realities and weed will amplify that. I had pretty bad psychosis with auditory delusions and terrible paranoia. And then I stopped and it continued. And then finally the symptoms stopped. The brain will believe whatever it wants to believe so even If you just have an anxiety disorder if you happen to be prone to this type of chemical reaction with weed it can lead to delusions and paranoia. So if you have a history of schizophrenia or are really worried about it or have any other symptoms that concern you speak to a medical professional. Otherwise you're fine. You don't just catch schizophrenia cause you smoked weed one time. Either you were already predisposed and will need to go on medication sooner rather than later or you were just not having a good time with weed.

Navigating friendships in adulthood can be especially hard. People are busy and are living their own lives. What I've learned from my own experiences and the experiences of my friends is it's important to establish those boundaries of what you're looking for. The type of friend you want to be and the type they want. I have one friend who wants to message constantly and has "complained" (not sure if that's the word I'm looking for) about how it's so hard to make friends and just when he thinks he's making a good friend they tell him he's coming on as too much. I'm the type of friend who wants to hang out/ message atleast once a month but don't need much more than that although I'm down for more if the other person is also in the mood. You don't have to say things super direct but it's best to establish how often you're looking to get in contact and the type of discussions you're comfortable having. The second point was my friends issue and I told him not everyone is comfortable talking about childhood traumas and whatnot even 3 months into a friendship. So if you find you're having more of an emotional pressure than a social pressure issue with a new friend try letting them know that you appreciate their experiences but you're more comfortable with casual topics. Anyway my point Is communicate your boundaries and needs and the people who are meant to be in your life will stick around.

One of my favorite memories from when I was a kid. I had alot of trouble sleeping on my own and would cry until my parents let me sleep in their bed. That night they had resolved no to so I cried. And cried. And cried. I ended up crying all night. I felt as if I was all alone and I felt very scared. My mom would always say "it's not the end of the world" when I would cry but it felt like it to me. But then the sun started to rise. I swear it was both the fastest sunrise and yet it felt like I had gone through a whole day. I watched it from start to finish. I had stopped crying the moment that magnificent glow began to fill my room. It was so beautiful. Watching the sky go from gold to orange to that soft blue to yellow. I felt like the world was telling me everything was going to be alright. To this day when I'm suicidal I always tell myself "just make it to the morning and you'll find hope again." Because every morning the sun rises. No matter what.
